sections.title: Touch #8 · nine rows inside the firewall
sections.question: Approve firewall touch #8 as exactly the nine rows below, and nothing wider? Approve = authorised for P3 objectives 1 and 5, with canvas_std back to diff 0 on commit. Amend = strike or add a row in the note. Discuss = hold.
sections.analysis:
• 1–3 conformance.py: check-sync and check_sync() beside _cli (:82); ConformanceReport.advisories, additive, printed as warnings that never move the exit code; the three v2.4.0 strings (:69 · :87 · :94), derived from STANDARD_VERSION.
  • 4 README.md, re-cut: pins :3 · :6 · :37 to v2.5.0; :8 is history; the counts at :9–:10 and :30 re-measured at the build; a check-sync usage block.
  • 5–6 tests: exits 0 / 1 / 2, a blind spot on every leg line, and the advisory field printed without moving the exit code. On a canvas whose digest is its prose: a typo reads source stale, topology fresh; a layout-only change reads both fresh, with rebuild named as unseen.
  • 7–8 corpus: all 7 arrow and both fromEnd values; coverage 12/40 today, the pin set to the build's measured figure. Rider, live since 8191348: manifest.json:142 still calls the ADR-004 fixture a byte-copy, and it is not one now.
  • 9 CHANGELOG: one entry, under a heading that cuts no Standard version.
  • Diff 0: validate.py · reserved.py · schema.py · roundtrip.py · __init__.py · the JSON Schema · certify.py · every spec. The gate pins (236, 22) and (15, 0) are re-derived outside, by stash and restore.

recommendation.rationale: Every file is named before the signature, so nothing lands under it unseen, and each row maps to a ruled item or a recorded residue.
key_factors: Rows 2–4 are the touch-#7 residue that LIP-0011 recorded
Rows 7–8 are queue ③ as you ruled it on 2026-10-16
risks: Rows 7–8 move gate pins; the new figures are measured at the build, never predicted
next_actions: Build in one touch after the signature and paste the gate line
Restore canvas_std to diff 0 on commit

sections.title: D-1 · Where check_sync() lives
sections.question: Where does check_sync() live? Approve = (i): in conformance.py beside the CLI, with no new package export, so __init__.py stays at diff 0. Amend = (ii): in roundtrip.py beside the two hash functions, plus an __all__ export; write “(ii)” in the note.
sections.analysis:
• (i) is the smallest touch: one file, and the CLI is the third-party face the mission names.
  • (ii) gives Python callers one function, at the cost of two more rows (roundtrip.py and __init__.py).
  • Measured: __init__.py already exports compute_sync_hash, compute_source_sha256 and advisories (touch #7), so a Python caller can run both legs today without (ii). An export can follow in a later touch if someone asks for one.

recommendation.rationale: Ship the face the mission names; add a Python export when a caller asks for one.
key_factors: Both legs are already callable from Python
risks: A Python caller re-implements the exit-code rule until an export exists
next_actions: Under (ii), add roundtrip.py and __init__.py to row 1 before the build

sections.title: D-2 · Does a topology mismatch fail?
sections.question: Does a topology mismatch fail check-sync? Approve = no: it prints as an advisory, and only a stale source leg exits 1. Amend = fail: a topology mismatch exits 1 too; write “fail” in the note.
sections.analysis:
• One canvas, one verdict. validate() reports the same mismatch as an advisory at both tiers (LIP-0011 D-1 (i), signed; spec A-6).
  • What the leg sees (design §6.3): the canvas against its own stored hash. It never reads the source, so it misses every source change, a topology change included, and any canvas edit that keeps the ids and pairs. An exit 0 earned on it alone says only that the canvas is consistent with itself.
  • The price, measured here at c313b8c: of 34 tracked canvases, 25 carry sync_hash at the canonical path and 3 of those carry sync.source_sha256. Under no and section 4, the other 22 exit 2, as do the 3 when run without --source; under fail, the 22 exit 0 or 1 on self-consistency alone.
  • Not the Terminal lever: you moved that clause to P4 on 2026-10-26.

recommendation.rationale: Keep the CLI and the validator on one verdict, and keep exit 0 meaning that a leg which read the source found it unchanged.
key_factors: Hardening later is a small, measured change
risks: Until producers stamp sync.source_sha256, most canvases exit 2 (22 of 25 here)
next_actions: Tests pin the exit code under the ruled reading
The P4 memos say what exit 2 means

sections.title: Exit 2 · when no failable leg ran
sections.question: Approve exit 2 when no leg that can fail has run, as well as on unreadable input? It extends the P3 Exit Gate's “exits 0/1”, so Approve also amends that wording, dated at the build and struck, not deleted. Amend = another rule in the note.
sections.analysis:
• The gap (design §6.2): read literally, §1 let a canvas with no digest and a fresh topology exit 0, though nothing that can fail had run.
  • The rule is already this vault's: gate #9 fails a pair it cannot run (D-O2-3), and a cross-check that cannot fail looks exactly like a cross-check that passed (P2b).
  • Which legs can fail is D-2's answer: under no, the source leg only; under fail, the topology leg too.
  • The codes: 0 = at least one failable leg ran and all read fresh · 1 = one read stale · 2 = unreadable input, or nothing failable ran. A leg that cannot run prints n/a with its reason.

recommendation.rationale: A run that checks nothing must not exit 0.
key_factors: Third parties can tell fresh from not checked
risks: A caller that reads any non-zero as stale will read exit 2 as stale; the usage block says what it means
next_actions: Tests pin exit 2 on every nothing-failable case
Amend the P3 Exit Gate wording at the build

sections.title: D-3 · No LIP: tooling and corpus only
sections.question: Confirm that touch #8 changes no Standard text and the Standard stays v2.5.0? Approve = no LIP. Amend = a LIP comes first and the touch waits; name the clause in the note.
sections.analysis:
• No spec file is in the nine rows: they are reference tooling, tests and corpus.
  • One edge, found while authoring this door: the conformance suite's §7 lists six report fields (standard_version · level_reached · declared_level · passed · failed · degradation). Row 2 gives the reference report a seventh, advisories. The report already carries ok (conformance.py:78), which comes from §1.1, not §7. A-6 already names the advisory and its reporter, canvas_std.advisories().
  • Approve reads §7 as what a report must carry, not all it may carry. If you read §7 as closed, two other routes remain: drop row 2's field and only print advisories (§7 untouched), or a §7 LIP first.
  • Under approve, row 9's entry cuts no Standard version.

recommendation.rationale: The Standard already defines advisories; row 2 makes the report carry them, additively.
key_factors: No spec file among the nine rows
A-6 already names the advisory and its reporter
risks: §7 lists six fields and the reference report would carry seven, until a later LIP says so
next_actions: If approved, the CHANGELOG entry names the §7 gap
If amended, draft the §7 LIP before the build
